data.one_liner: Unified offline‑first repository that syncs SQLite with remote providers.
data.what_it_does: It routes data fetching through a memory cache, a local SQLite provider, and a remote provider (REST/GraphQL). Policies let you control when to read/write locally or remotely and it queues failed remote writes for later sync.
use_when: You need reliable offline support with automatic sync to a backend
You want a single API for CRUD that works both online and offline
Your app already uses Brick for other domains
avoid_when: The app only needs simple network calls without local persistence
You prefer a lightweight solution without code generation
You are not using SQLite or Brick elsewhere
strengths: Automatic offline‑first sync and policy control
Supports memory cache, SQLite queue for failed requests
Integrates with Brick codegen for models and providers
weaknesses: Adds build_runner step and code‑gen complexity
Tied to Brick ecosystem, not a generic solution
May be overkill for small apps
data.setup_notes: Add brick_core, brick_sqlite and other deps, run `flutter pub run build_runner build`, configure local and remote providers in your repository.

alternatives.name: http
alternatives.why_pick_it: For simple REST calls without offline caching or SQLite integration
